questions.question: Can the Vickers hardness of 675 Hv in CoCrFeNiTi HEAs be reproduced in a single-phase FCC composition by eliminating the BCC phase, or does the BCC phase contribute significantly to the hardening mechanism via solid solution strengthening?
questions.rationale: Distinguishes whether the high hardness is driven by the specific multiphase architecture (FCC/BCC) or general grain refinement, influencing phase design strategies.
questions.decision_use: Informs whether to target a single-phase microstructure or maintain a multiphase composition for strength.
answer_requirements: Synthesize a CoCrFeNiTi alloy with 100% FCC structure (e.g., by adjusting VEC)
Compare Vickers hardness and yield stress to the 675 Hv baseline
evidence_spans: The milled powder exhibited nanocrystalline solid solution microstructure with grain sizes below 48 nm, composed of 83% face–centered cubic (FCC) and 17% body–centered cubic (BCC) phases.
This increasing in hardness resulted from grain refinement and enhanced dislocation density due to prolonged milling.
